title: add RAG agent templates, tool-calling examples, and quickstart docs
author: Avery Chen
description:
Motivation: Provide first-class, production-oriented examples and quickstarts for RAG-based agents and tool-calling workflows. These examples are intended to help engineers adopt Redwood's agent APIs and tool-calling primitives quickly, demonstrate recommended prompt/chain patterns, and provide ready-to-run quickstarts for the docs site and redwood-examples.

What this PR does: adds a set of RAG agent templates (prompt templates + retrieval wiring), three tool-calling example integrations (calendar, search, metrics), and docs site quickstarts with runnable snippets and step-by-step instructions. The examples emphasize: 1) secure tool invocation patterns, 2) predictable retrieval and caching settings, and 3) testable prompt templates suitable for evals.

Files added/changed: new quickstarts under redwood-docs/content/quickstarts/rag-agents, example code under redwood-examples/rag-agents/{basic,tool-calls,enterprise}, and small docs-site configuration updates for sidebars and TOC. Also includes a small fix to the agent SDK helper that ensures deterministic tool name resolution when tool namespaces overlap.

Checklist: - [x] Add RAG agent prompt templates and template docs - [x] Add 3 tool-calling example projects with README and tests - [x] Hook quickstarts into docs site navigation - [x] Add smoke tests and CI job for examples - [x] Run docs-site build and fix rendering issues found during review

How to run locally: follow quickstart README: clone redwood-examples, cd to the example folder, install dependencies (yarn/pip), set REDWOOD_API_KEY (or run with dev server), and run the provided start script. Each example contains mocked tool adapters for local testing and instructions to swap in real integrations.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the agent runtime surface untouched only the SDK helper for tool name resolution is a minimal behavioral tweak and covered by unit tests. The quickstarts include small end-to-end smoke tests that run against our internal dev stack; those tests are skipped in external CI unless REDWOOD_TEST_DEVSTACK is provided.
